turns.learner: Hello! I want to practise reading between the lines. I think I am good at it already.
turns.tutor:
Hello! Great, let's try. To "infer" means to find an idea from clues in the text. Example: "He wore a coat and gloves." Clue: coat, gloves. So we infer: it was cold.

Now you try. Yuki checked her notes again and again. Her hands shook as the audience took their seats. How does Yuki probably feel: excited, nervous or sleepy? Tell me the clue too.

turns.learner: Excited! The audience is coming, so she is happy and her hands shake because she is very excited for the show.
turns.tutor:
Good try, and you used a clue. But look: does the text say she is happy? No. "Happy" is a guess. The clues are: she checked her notes again and again, and her hands shook. People do this when they are worried before a talk. So nervous has more evidence.

Try again: Was the shop busy? The queue reached the door. People waited with full baskets while the staff hurried between the tills. Yes or no? Which clue?

turns.learner: Yes, busy. The queue reached the door and the staff hurried. Maybe it is a sale day, so everyone wants cheap food.
turns.tutor:
Yes, busy is right, and your clues are good: the queue and the hurrying staff. But "sale day" and "cheap food" are not in the text. There is no clue for them. Stop at what the evidence shows: the shop was busy.

New text: Sara looked at the sky and took her umbrella. Then she put on her boots. What can we infer, and which clues support it?

turns.learner: It will rain. Umbrella and boots are the clues. Maybe she is going to a wedding after, so she wants to look nice.
turns.tutor:
Yes! It will probably rain. Clues: she looked at the sky, took an umbrella, put on boots. Very good.

But again, the wedding idea has no clue in the text. Here is a check you can use: "Which words in the text show this?" If you cannot point to words, it is a guess.

Try this: Tom's plate was empty. He smiled and rubbed his stomach. What can we infer? Point to the words.

turns.learner: He ate everything and he is full. The words are empty plate, smiled, rubbed stomach. I think his mother cooked it, because it was tasty.
turns.tutor:
Excellent! He ate everything and feels full and happy. You pointed to the exact words: empty plate, smiled, rubbed stomach.

"His mother cooked it" is not in the text. Who cooked? No clue. Can you say which part of your answer has evidence, and which part is a guess?

turns.learner: Evidence is he ate and is full. The guess is his mother cooked. But I think it is still probably true, mothers cook.
turns.tutor:
Well done: you separated evidence from guess. That is the key skill.

It could be true, but "could be" is not "the text suggests". Tom's father, a friend or a restaurant could also have made it. With no clue, we do not choose one. A good inference needs evidence in the text.

Next time, ask: which words show this? Great work today!
